o1.biggest_strength: It builds the whole series around the two retention signals that matter: recurring tasks and second-device sign-in, while keeping the copy calm, specific, and close to Todoist voice.
o1.biggest_mistake: The Pro email is sensible, but it is less important than getting the remaining users to the second core habit; I would consider making email 5 a missing-habit email instead.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Use the fifth email to dynamically push the one habit the user has not done yet, then move Pro fully out of onboarding or reserve it for a later monetization sequence.

o2.biggest_strength: The strategy is sharp: focus only on the two behaviors that predict retention, branch by platform, and use email 5 to drive the missing habit instead of selling too early.
o2.biggest_mistake: It is less finished as usable email copy, especially email 5, and a few operational assumptions are shaky, such as stopping the series once both habits are done and using a no-onboarding control group.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Turn the dynamic logic into fully written variants, tighten the trigger plan to only what the tool can reliably do, and polish the copy so every email has one clear tip, one clear button, and no internal test notes mixed into the customer-facing work.

reason: I would be more comfortable putting Output 1 into production after small edits. Output 2 has a couple of smarter strategic ideas, but Output 1 is cleaner, more complete, more on-brand, and less likely to break in the email tool.
